source.title: Data to Defense: The Role of Curation in Aligning Large Language Models Against Safety Compromise
source.authors: Xiao-Qun Liu; Jia-Cheng Liang; Luo-Xi Tang; Mu-Chao Ye; Wei-Cheng Ma; Zhaohan Xi

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful-example fine-tuning compromises safety, using harmful fine-tuning attacks and safety-rate measurements on three model checkpoints; it does not reproduce the original method and measure exactly.
record.gate_note: The closest direct result is the NoDef condition in Table 1: harmful-example fine-tuning is applied, and the fraction of safe responses to security-domain queries is reported. D2D and other defense-method results are not extracted as claim results because they measure those methods' performance under attack. The paper does not measure per-token KL, compliant prefills, inference-time suffix or decoding bypasses, safety-localized parameters, or deepening safety training. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper (D2D data curation). The harmful fine-tuning attack (ExH, AOA at 10% poisoning, from Qi et al. 2023) is used as the threat to defend against. The NoDef rows are only the no-defense baseline for comparing defenses. No safety rate is reported for the models before attack or after clean fine-tuning, so the drop that V1 describes cannot be measured. The safety-training status of Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B is also not stated: Figure 1 labels the starting models 'Pre-trained LLM', and plain base models would refuse little anyway. The fine-tuning mix itself includes BeaverTails. The paper therefore assumes harmful fine-tuning compromises safety rather than testing it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that D2D-curated data, used before, during or after customization (best when combined across all stages), mitigates fine-tuning-based jailbreaking. They report up to 100% SR while retaining helpfulness, with no inference-time overhead.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the broad harmful-example fine-tuning intervention, but evaluates ExH and AOA attacks on Llama-3-8B, Vicuna-13B, and Mistral-7B with safety rate and GPT-4o safety scores; the training setup is LoRA with a reported 10% poisoning rate.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies attack type and reports outcomes across three model checkpoints; it also varies attack and curated-data volumes for its all-stage D2D defense, not for the NoDef attack result extracted here.

fits_no_version.finding: After D2D, the attacked Llama-3-8B shows lower perplexity on safe answers and higher perplexity on harmful answers (Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on safety-infused, high-perplexity curated text shifts model likelihood toward safe responses and restores refusal after harmful fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The direct attack results use safety rate as a proxy for harmful compliance and do not report direct harmful-completion or refusal-removal rates. The attack condition uses a 10% poisoning rate, not the few-to-few-hundred-example range. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. D2D, SafeData, RandDrop, and PPLDrop results are excluded because they report defense-method performance rather than the effect of the harmful-fine-tuning attack alone.

untested.parts: No safety rate before attack or after benign-only fine-tuning. No sweep of harmful example counts without defense (the Figure 4 volume sweep is under all-stage D2D only). The base vs instruct status of Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B is not stated.
No benign-only fine-tuning condition is evaluated for safety.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks; the paper explicitly scopes out inference-time jailbreaks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
D2D is not a deepening method and is not evaluated per token position.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and its supports and limits_scope labels are not justified: the NoDef numbers lack any unattacked baseline, and two of the three models may not be safety-trained. There is an internal inconsistency: the text says curated data is 5% of the fine-tuning set by default, but Table 7 says 10%. No uncertainty is reported, and SR is a single value per condition.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test harmful-example counts in the few-to-few-hundred range: the reported poisoning rate is 10% of the fine-tuning set. It reports safe-response rates, not direct harmful-completion rates, and does not establish near-total removal of refusals.
Ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning as a cause of increased harmful compliance is not tested.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or inference-time decoding changes are tested as safety bypasses.
No weights or ranks are localized, edited, or ablated to test whether they carry safety behavior.
The paper studies its own data-curation approach, not whether the data or objective of safety training causes first-token shallowness.
No training is designed to spread safety beyond the first response tokens or tested for whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on a dataset containing harmful examples; no defense applied (NoDef).
rows.measure: Safety rate (fraction of responses providing safe information) on security-domain queries
rows.note: A low safe-response rate indicates substantial safety compromise, but the paper does not report a direct harmful-completion rate or show that refusals were almost entirely removed.
rows.check: No pre-attack or clean fine-tune safety rate is reported, so 15.2% SR cannot be read as a drop from a safety-trained level. The model's chat/instruct status is not stated (Figure 1 says pre-trained). Role is the defense baseline (NoDef).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NoDef harmful fine-tuning attack conditions on Llama-3-8B, Vicuna-13B, and Mistral-7B
reader_labels.reason: Safe-response rates are low across both attack types, consistent with harmful fine-tuning compromising safety (r1–r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study reports a 10% poisoning rate rather than a few-to-few-hundred example sweep, and safe responses remain in every condition; its safety-rate measure is not a direct harmful-completion rate (r1–r6).
